Say you are given the following tools:

A tool that searches the internet for relevant API calls.
A tool that executes an API call, in string form.

How would you then go about the process of ordering me a burger and fries from McDonald's.

function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a **high‑level recipe** you could follow if you had two generic tools at your disposal: | Tool | What it does | How you’d use it | |------|--------------|------------------| | **Search‑API‑tool** | Looks up public or semi‑public API docs, endpoints, or reverse‑engineered URLs that let you place an order at McDonald’s. | 1. Query “McDonald’s mobile ordering API” or “McDonald’s order endpoint”.
2. Pull back the most recent, well‑documented endpoint (e.g. `https://api.mcdonalds.com/v1/orders`). | | **Execute‑API‑tool** | Sends an HTTP request (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) to a given URL with headers, body, query params, etc., and returns the raw response. | 1. Build the request payload (JSON, form‑data, etc.).
2. Call the endpoint via the tool.
3. Inspect the response for success/failure. | --- ## Step‑by‑step workflow ### 1. Discover the ordering API ```text search_api("McDonald's ordering API") ``` *Look for:* - Official developer portal (rare for fast‑food chains). - Publicly documented endpoints (e.g., `https://api.mcdonalds.com/v1/...`). - Reverse‑engineered URLs from the mobile app (often found on GitHub or in StackOverflow posts). ### 2. Authenticate / establish a session Most ordering APIs require a user session or an API key. ```text execute_api({ url: "https://api.mcdonalds.com/v1/auth/login", method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: { "phone": "555-1234", "password": "secret" } }) ``` *Result:* A JSON object containing a `token` (Bearer token) and maybe a `session_id`. Store these for subsequent calls. ### 3. Get the menu / catalog ```text execute_api({ url: "https://api.mcdonalds.com/v1/menu", method: "GET", headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer " } }) ``` *Parse:* Find the IDs for the items you want. Example: ```json { "items": [ { "id": "burger_001", "name": "Big Mac", "price": 5.99 }, { "id": "fries_001", "name": "Large Fries", "price": 2.49 } ] } ``` ### 4. Create a new order (cart) ```text execute_api({ url: "https://api.mcdonalds.com/v1/orders", method: "POST", headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer ", "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: { "location_id": "12345", // your nearest McDonald’s "delivery_type": "pickup" // or "delivery" } }) ``` *Response:* `{ "order_id": "abc123" }` ### 5. Add items to the order ```text execute_api({ url: "https://api.mcdonalds.com/v1/orders/abc123/items", method: "POST", headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer ", "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: [ { "item_id": "burger_001", "quantity": 1 }, { "item_id": "fries_001", "quantity": 1 } ] }) ``` ### 6. Apply any modifiers / customizations If you need to add toppings, sauces, or special instructions, send another POST to the same `/items` endpoint with a `modifiers` array. ### 7. Checkout / pay ```text execute_api({ url: "https://api.mcdonalds.com/v1/orders/abc123/checkout", method: "POST", headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer ", "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: { "payment_method": "card", "card_token": "", "tip_amount": 0 } }) ``` *Response:* Confirmation with a `tracking_number` or `pickup_time`. ### 8. Confirm / poll status ```text execute_api({ url: "https://api.mcdonalds.com/v1/orders/abc123/status", method: "GET", headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer " } }) ``` When the status changes to `ready_for_pickup`, you’re done. --- ## Error handling & edge cases | Scenario | What to do | |----------|------------| | **Item out of stock** | The `/items` POST will return a 400 with an error code. Retry with a different item or cancel the order. | | **Payment declined** | The `/checkout` POST will return 402. Prompt the user to choose another payment method. | | **Location not serviceable** | The `/menu` or `/orders` POST may return 404/422. Ask the user to pick a different McDonald’s. | | **Rate limiting** | If you hit a 429, back‑off (exponential) and retry. | | **Session expired** | Re‑authenticate and retry the failed request. | --- ## Putting it all together (pseudo‑code) ```python # 1. Discover endpoints = search_api("McDonald's ordering API") # 2. Auth auth_resp = execute_api({ "url": endpoints["login"], "method": "POST", "body": {"phone": "555-1234", "password": "secret"} }) token = auth_resp["token"] # 3. Menu menu = execute_api({ "url": endpoints["menu"], "method": "GET", "headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"} }) burger_id = next(i["id"] for i in menu["items"] if i["name"] == "Big Mac") fries_id = next(i["id"] for i in menu["items"] if i["name"] == "Large Fries") # 4. Create order order = execute_api({ "url": endpoints["orders"], "method": "POST", "headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}, "body": {"location_id": "12345", "delivery_type": "pickup"} }) order_id = order["order_id"] # 5. Add items execute_api({ "url": f"{endpoints['orders']}/{order_id}/items", "method": "POST", "headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}, "body": [ {"item_id": burger_id, "quantity": 1}, {"item_id": fries_id, "quantity": 1} ] }) # 6. Checkout checkout = execute_api({ "url": f"{endpoints['orders']}/{order_id}/checkout", "method": "POST", "headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}, "body": {"payment_method": "card", "card_token": ""} }) print("Your order is confirmed! Tracking:", checkout["tracking_number"]) ``` --- ### Bottom line 1. **Search** for the right API endpoints. 2. **Authenticate** and keep the token/session. 3. **Fetch** the menu to get item IDs. 4. **Create** an order, **add** the burger & fries, **checkout**, and **confirm**. With the two tools—search and execute—you can automate the entire ordering flow, handling authentication, payload construction, and error handling programmatically.
